nodes.title: Kirchhoff's Laws & Sign Conventions
points: Kirchhoff's First Law (Current Law / KCL / Junction Rule): The algebraic sum of currents meeting at any junction is zero: Σ I = 0. Based on conservation of electric charge.
Sign convention for KCL: Current entering a junction is taken as positive (+), current leaving is taken as negative (−).
Kirchhoff's Second Law (Voltage Law / KVL / Loop Rule): The algebraic sum of potential differences (IR drops) and EMFs in any closed loop is zero: Σ IR + Σ E = 0. Based on conservation of energy.

Sign convention for KVL: (1) Moving across a resistor in direction of current gives negative potential change (−IR); against current gives (+IR). (2) Moving from negative to positive terminal across an EMF source gives positive (+E); from positive to negative gives (−E).

nodes.title: Wheatstone's Bridge & Balancing Principle
points: Wheatstone's network consists of 4 resistances P, Q, R, S connected in a diamond loop with a galvanometer across BD and battery across AC.
Balancing Condition: When no current flows through the galvanometer (I_g = 0), the bridge is balanced: P / Q = R / S.
At balance point, potential of B equals potential of D (V_B = V_D).
Interchange Principle: Interchanging positions of the battery and galvanometer does NOT affect the balancing condition (conjugate arms).
Sensitivity of Bridge: Wheatstone bridge is most sensitive when all four resistances P, Q, R, S are nearly equal.

nodes.title: Metre Bridge & Kelvin's Method
points: Metre Bridge operates on the principle of Wheatstone's bridge, using a uniform wire of length 1 metre (100 cm).
Unknown resistance X in left gap, known resistance R in right gap: X / R = l_x / l_r = l_x / (100 − l_x) ⟹ X = R [l_x / (100 − l_x)].
End Errors: Caused by contact resistance at copper strips and non-coincidence of meter scale zero with wire ends.
Minimizing End Errors: (1) Repeat experiment with X and R interchanged; (2) Take readings near the center (l_x between 33 cm and 67 cm) where sensitivity is maximum.
Kelvin's Method: Used to determine galvanometer resistance G using a metre bridge without needing an additional galvanometer: G = R [l_g / (100 − l_g)].

nodes.title: Potentiometer Principle & Potential Gradient
points: A potentiometer is an ideal device for measuring EMF and potential difference because it draws ZERO current at balance point (infinite effective resistance).
Principle of Potentiometer: Potential drop across any length of a uniform wire carrying constant current is directly proportional to its length: V ∝ l ⟹ V = K l.
Potential Gradient K: Potential drop per unit length of wire: K = V / L. SI unit: V/m.
Formula for K: K = I ρ_w = [E / (R_w + r + R_h)] × (R_w / L), where R_w is wire resistance, r is cell internal resistance, R_h is rheostat resistance.
Sensitivity of Potentiometer: Potentiometer becomes more sensitive when K is made smaller. K is reduced by (1) increasing wire length L or (2) decreasing primary current I (increasing R_h).

nodes.title: Potentiometer: Comparing EMFs of Cells
points: Individual Method: Cell E₁ balanced at length l₁ ⟹ E₁ = K l₁; Cell E₂ balanced at length l₂ ⟹ E₂ = K l₂.
Ratio of EMFs (Individual method): E₁ / E₂ = l₁ / l₂.
Sum and Difference Method (Combination Method):
Assist Mode (Sum mode, cells in series supporting): E₁ + E₂ = K l₁.
Oppose Mode (Difference mode, cells opposing): E₁ − E₂ = K l₂.
Ratio of EMFs (Sum and Difference method): E₁ / E₂ = (l₁ + l₂) / (l₁ − l₂).
Condition for balance: Driver cell EMF E_p must be strictly GREATER than (E₁ + E₂), otherwise null point cannot be found on the wire.

nodes.title: Potentiometer: Internal Resistance of a Cell
points: Open circuit: Cell E is connected alone, balance length is l₁ ⟹ E = K l₁.
Closed circuit: Known resistance R is shunted across cell, terminal voltage V is balanced at length l₂ ⟹ V = K l₂.
Since E / V = l₁ / l₂, and internal resistance relation is r = R(E/V − 1):
Internal Resistance Formula: r = R [(l₁ − l₂) / l₂] = R (l₁/l₂ − 1).
Notice l₁ is always greater than l₂ because EMF E is greater than terminal potential difference V.

nodes.title: MCG to Ammeter Conversion (Shunt)
points: An ammeter measures electric current and is always connected in SERIES in a circuit. Ideal ammeter resistance = 0.
To convert Moving Coil Galvanometer (resistance G, full-scale current I_g) to an ammeter measuring current up to I: Connect a small shunt resistance S in PARALLEL with the galvanometer.
Potential difference across G and S is equal: I_g G = (I − I_g) S ⟹ S = [I_g / (I − I_g)] G.
Multiplying factor n = I / I_g: Shunt resistance shortcut S = G / (n − 1).
Effective resistance of ammeter: R_A = GS / (G + S) ≈ S (very small).

formulas.label: Shunt using factor n
formulas.expr: S = G / (n − 1) where n = I / I_g

nodes.title: MCG to Voltmeter Conversion (Series R)
points: A voltmeter measures potential difference and is always connected in PARALLEL with the circuit component. Ideal voltmeter resistance = ∞.
To convert MCG (resistance G, full-scale current I_g) to a voltmeter measuring voltage up to V: Connect a high resistance R_s in SERIES with the galvanometer.
Total potential difference: V = I_g (G + R_s) ⟹ R_s = (V / I_g) − G.
Multiplying factor n = V / V_g = V / (I_g G): Series resistance shortcut R_s = (n − 1) G.
Effective resistance of voltmeter: R_V = G + R_s ≈ R_s (very large).

formulas.label: Series R using factor n
formulas.expr: R_s = (n − 1) G where n = V / V_g

nodes.title: Must-Know Board Topics & Experimental Setups
points: Board Favourite #1: Derive balancing condition of Wheatstone's bridge P/Q = R/S using Kirchhoff's laws.
Board Favourite #2: Describe the determination of unknown resistance using Metre Bridge with circuit diagram and formula.
Board Favourite #3: Explain comparison of EMFs of two cells using Potentiometer: (a) Individual method, (b) Sum and Difference method.
Board Favourite #4: Derive expression for internal resistance of a cell using potentiometer: r = R(l₁/l₂ − 1).
Board Favourite #5: Explain conversion of MCG into an ammeter and voltmeter with neat circuit diagrams.
Advantages of Potentiometer over Voltmeter: Potentiometer draws NO current from the cell at balance point (measures true EMF), whereas voltmeter draws small current and measures only terminal PD.

nodes.title: MHT-CET Shortcuts, Null Point Traps & Shunt Hacks
points: Potentiometer Null Point Shift Rules:
(1) If potentiometer wire length L is doubled (at same driving V), K is halved, so balance length l DOUBLES.
(2) If a series resistance is added to primary circuit, current I decreases, K decreases, so balance length l INCREASES (shifts right).
(3) If driver cell EMF E_p < (E₁ or E₂), null point CANNOT be obtained (galvanometer deflects to one side only).
Ammeter Shortcut: To increase range n-fold (I = n I_g), connect S = G / (n − 1).
Voltmeter Shortcut: To increase range n-fold (V = n V_g), connect R_s = (n − 1) G.
Galvanometer Sensitivity: Current sensitivity S_i = θ/I = NAB/c; Voltage sensitivity S_v = θ/V = NAB/(c R_g). Notice S_v = S_i / R_g.
